source_ref: OSF dqw9f (public node; API reports no node licence): Studies In Main Text/Study 2 Data and Code/Study 2 Data no ID.sav (https://osf.io/download/hymb6/, sha256 390e7966...65b27f); Supplemental Studies/Study S1a Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/5p78v/, sha256 ceefe3a6...503f33), S1b (https://osf.io/download/8j3em/, sha256 55f1616c...e6e7ea), S1c (https://osf.io/download/2knxu/, sha256 4a5debaf...d9142e), S2a (https://osf.io/download/j7bu9/, sha256 64c2f427...3175ce), S2b (https://osf.io/download/6501ed786d1e89617115155a/, sha256 37cf92d0...ba05dd), S2c (https://osf.io/download/6501f901f3dcd16832ddd406/, sha256 77e72d25...e4732e) -- SPSS variable and value labels of certain1-3 (Study 2, S1c, S2c), certain1/certain2 (S1a, S1b, S2a) and cert1/certain2 (S2b); the studies' own .sps syntax; data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py for the code derivation and the S2c recode. Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read in all seven .sav files (OSF sha256s match the API listing). Code derivation: certain1-3 ARE the source column names in Study 2, S1c and S2c; certain_item1/certain_item2 are a fixed rename in the script (_cert1) of certain1/certain2 in S1a, S1b, S2a and of cert1/certain2 in S2b -- mechanical, so exempt from Step 5b and no verification files. (S2b also carries an unlabelled column certain1 identical to cert1 in all 340 rows; the script reads cert1, so nothing is lost.) TWO DESIGNS UNDER ONE TABLE (itemcov_design): Study 2 and S1c asked three differently worded global questions after the whole intelligence-beliefs block (labels character-identical in the two files); S2c used one identically worded rating after each of its three belief items, so its certain1/2/3 share the item codes of the global questions but not their wording. Following the batch_644-646 convention, item_text for certain1-3 carries both verbatim labels prefixed Studies 2 and S1c (cov_study = 1, 4): / Study S2c (cov_study = 7): and joined by " | " (prefixes and separator are IRW's). certain_item1/2 are the same per-response wording in all four studies that carry them and ship unprefixed. Per the .sav column order, certain_item1 follows the belief statement You have a certain amount of intelligence, and you can't really do much to change it. and certain_item2 follows Your intelligence is something about you that you can't change very much. (IQbelief1T1/IQbelief1T2); S2c certain1/2/3 follow IQbelief1T1/2T1/3T1. That referent is stated in public_note, not written into item_text. OPTIONS: Study 2/S1c value labels 1="Not at all1", 7="Very much7" (digit fused to the label); S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b 1="1 - Not at all", 7="7 - Very much"; S2c 1="1 - Very Certain", 7="7 - Very Uncertain". S2C IS REVERSED FOR THIS SCALE: the script writes S2c as 8-resp (itemcov_recoded=1 on all 2379 S2c rows, 0 elsewhere), and the authors' own S2c syntax does the same (compute certain = mean.1((8-certain1), (8-certain2), (8-certain3))). So live resp 1 = low certainty, 7 = high certainty in every study. Route 9, all 17 study x item count vectors match source = live, e.g. Study 2 certain1 9/27/62/141/261/196/142, S2b cert1 -> certain_item1 4/5/11/41/80/100/99; S2c certain1 source 184/156/153/113/112/48/27 -> live 27/48/112/113/153/156/184 (exact reversal). Direction cross-check: raw certainty correlates with belief extremity |IQbelief-4| at +0.34 (Study 2), +0.48 (S1c), +0.42..+0.60 (S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b) but -0.48..-0.54 in S2c, so the S2c printed 1 = Very Certain labels are correct and the recode is right. option_text for certain1-3 names both studies' anchors at resp 1 (Not at all | Very Uncertain) and 7 (Very much | Very Certain) with the same prefixes; certain_item1/2 get Not at all / Very much. Number prefixes/suffixes stripped from all anchors (they would be wrong for the recoded S2c rows); resp 2-6 carry only their own digit in every source and are left blank. No instructions text in any .sav or .sps; left blank. Rights: study-authored items, no stated restriction located (silence = permission). The S2b .sps download returned an OSF 500; not needed, labels are in the .sav.
public_note: Two designs share this table: Study 2 and Study S1c (cov_study = 1, 4) asked three global questions after all the intelligence-belief items, while Studies S1a, S1b, S2a, S2b (certain_item1-2) and S2c (certain1-3) asked How certain do you feel about the response that you just provided? right after each belief item (itemcov_design), so certain1-3 carry two wordings labelled by study; responses run 1 = low to 7 = high certainty in all studies, Study S2c having been reverse-recoded from its printed 1 = Very Certain order (itemcov_recoded = 1).
